chunks: Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the obligatory elements in the salat, and he said: 'The time, and the purity, and the qibla, and the facing, and the ruku', and the sujud, and the supplication.' I said, 'What about what is besides that?' He said: 'A sunnah within an obligation.'

key_terms.التوجه: Tawajjuh — the facing/orientation at the start of prayer; associated with the opening takbir
key_terms.الطهور: Ritual purity (taharah) — encompasses wudu, ghusl, and tayammum as prerequisites for salat
key_terms.الفرض: Obligatory element, fard — what is legally required in the prayer
key_terms.القبلة: Qibla — the direction of the Ka'ba in Mecca toward which Muslims pray
key_terms.سنة في فريضة: Sunnah within an obligation — recommended practices that are part of an obligatory act

ai.seo_question: What are the obligatory elements of salat according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Zurara ibn A'yan, one of the most eminent jurists among the companions of the Imams, asked Imam al-Baqir (AS) to enumerate the obligatory (fard) elements of salat. The Imam listed seven: the prayer time, ritual purity (taharah), facing the qibla, the opening facing (tawajjuh/takbirat al-ihram), bowing (ruku'), prostration (sujud), and supplication (du'a/tashahhud). When Zurara asked about everything else in the prayer, the Imam declared it all 'sunnah within an obligation' — meaning recommended practices embedded within the obligatory framework. This hadith became foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing the pillars (arkaan) from the recommended acts (sunan) of salat.

en.hubeali: Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the necessities regarding the Salāt. So heasws said: ‘The timing, and the cleanliness, and the Qiblah, and the concentration, and the Rukū, and the Sajdah, and the supplication’. I said, ‘What is besides that?’ Heasws said: ‘A Sunnah among the necessities’.
en.sarwar: 5. Hammad has narrated from Hariz from Zurarah from who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about what is obligatory in Salah (prayer).
He (the Imam) said, ‘Time, al-Tahur (cleansing), facing al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah), paying attention, al-Ruku‘, al-Sujud and praying. The rest are optional in an obligatory duty.’”
